                    ### Question
                    A 72-year-old male visits his gastroenterologist for a check-up one year following resection of a 2-cm malignant lesion in his sigmoid colon. Serum levels of which of the following can be used in this patient to test for cancer recurrence?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Alpha-fetoprotein
opb. Carcinoembryonic antigen
opc. Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125)
opd. Gamma glutamyl transferase
ope. CA-19-9 tumor marker

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is a well-established marker for colorectal cancer and is commonly used to monitor for recurrence after treatment. This aligns with the consensus that CEA is the most appropriate serum marker for detecting recurrence in a patient with a history of colorectal cancer. Alpha-fetoprotein is primarily a marker for liver cancer and is not used for colorectal cancer. Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125) is associated with ovarian cancer and not relevant for colorectal cancer. Gamma glutamyl transferase is a liver enzyme and not a specific marker for any cancer type. CA-19-9 is a marker for pancreatic cancer and may sometimes be elevated in colorectal cancer, but it is not the primary marker for monitoring recurrence in colorectal cancer. Therefore, the best option for monitoring cancer recurrence in this patient is carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA).
